assertion_analysis.tests/standard_names/test_campaign.py:75: fails if the runner stops taking its pre-drain read before clear_quarantine, because the expected event list begins with fetch:a; it does not fail on what that read is used for.
assertion_analysis.tests/standard_names/test_campaign_conve: fails if _split_name_accepted stops excluding a reviewed member, because eligible would then contain all four ids; it does not fail if measure_batch's drift comparison is removed, because the batch it hands over holds only accepted names.

does not fail if the prior_rows comparison at campaign.py:670 is removed: the fixture's post-drain stage (reviewed) is not accepted, so the unrepaired absolute check reports the same drift; it fails only if the drift clause itself is deleted.

fails if any score-based acceptance is reintroduced at campaign.py:671-673, because accepted would read 2 and the literal 50.00% (1/2 touched) halt string would not be produced; logs-pinned-truth-mutation.log records exactly that reinstatement reddening this test alone.

findings.text: non-blocking: test_member_the_drain_moves_out_of_accepted_still_halts cannot fail on the defect it names. Its fixture moves one name from accepted to reviewed, which the pre-repair absolute-stage check also reports as drift, so reinstating that check — or deleting the prior_rows comparison at campaign.py:656-668 — leaves name_drift == ['moved_away'], touched 0 and the drift halt all intact. The drift repair therefore has no behavioural guard: no test calls measure_batch with a member whose non-accepted stage is unchanged between the two reads (test_member_outside_accepted_before_the_drain_is_skipped_not_drift filters those out of batch_ids first), so the false halt fixed here is pinned only by the planning split at harmonize.py:1313. Add a case carrying an unchanged reviewed member in batch_ids with prior_rows supplied and assert name_drift == [].

non-blocking: the plan's skipped and docs_eligible keys are written and never read. `git grep` over the head tree for docs_eligible finds only this construction site, and no CLI or apply path prints or stores plan['skipped'], so `sn harmonize --apply` reports a family applying with fewer members and no record of which were excluded or what stage they carry. The brief asks for exactly that report ('report it as skipped, with its stage, so the family's outcome names it'), so the second half of the planning repair is data on an internal dict rather than anything an operator or the run's outcome can see.

non-blocking: the tests table says the first test asserts 'measure_batch over the eligible pair yields no drift, 2 touched, 2 accepted'. At the reviewed head that test asserts no accepted count at all (the assertion was removed in 5d319309d) and the landed rule yields accepted == 1, because the held member is reviewed. Two is the number the withdrawn score-based rule produced, so this row describes code the same commit removed and contradicts the fragment's own 'a held document is not accepted' narrative at line 177.

non-blocking: the sentence says the excluded members are 'carried in the plan under skipped with their stage, so the family's outcome names them', but no consumer of that key exists anywhere in imas_codex/, so the outcome never names them; the sentence overclaims what landed, in the same way as the table row at line 167.

non-blocking: baseline_suite and after_suite are prose sentences rather than the JSON objects the dispatch contract asks for (revision, command, exit_status, log_path, completed, failure_count, failure_ids). completed has no value at all, so both arms read as unreadable by shape even though the logs behind them are complete and reconcile; the failure delta had to be re-derived from logs-gate-base.log and logs-gate-head.log to produce added_failure_ids here.

non-blocking: the tests field is a description of the gate ('two-arm gate over 22 files covering campaign and harmonize, from separate git archive trees ...') rather than the literal command a shell was handed, so the promotion gate receipt cannot be filled from it; the real command exists in each log's `# command:` header, which the fallback would find, but the field as written is a sentence, not a re-runnable command.

justifications.durability: test_campaign_convergence_gate.py:128 asserts drift for a member moved off accepted, which the unrepaired absolute-stage check reports identically, so deleting the prior_rows comparison leaves all three tests green; only :150 pins a rule the old code violates, and plan_family_applies' skipped list and anchor-deferral have no test at all.
justifications.evidence: logs-gate-base.log and logs-gate-head.log each open with revision, tree, the literal command and module.__file__, and close EXIT=1 at 4 failed/230 passed and 1 failed/233 passed, from which the added ids are none, but the done_when's acceptance-count clause is unmet and the measure text was never amended.
justifications.fit: The added symbols _name_stages (harmonize.py:1235) and _split_name_accepted (:1248) are named for their mechanism, carry no plan or ticket labels, follow the module's deferred-import and gc.query idiom, and all three touched Python files pass ruff check and ruff format --check at the head revision.
justifications.goal_fidelity: campaign.py:656-668 compares the post-drain stage against prior_stage before deciding drift, and harmonize.py:1331 builds each batch from eligible_ids only, so neither the false drift nor a non-accepted member entering a docs-only batch can recur; the acceptance halt is left standing under the coordinator's recorded ruling at resume-1-advice.txt:1-2. The planning skip is not surfaced anywhere, so the goal's second half — naming the excluded member — is only half delivered.
justifications.reuse: The eligibility split has no owner, but _name_stages (harmonize.py:1235) re-reads a column that campaign.py:741 (_REFRESH_QUERY / default_fetch_refreshed) already owns a by-ids reader for and that families.py:1041 _family_member_collect could carry in one line, so the duplication rule applies rather than a genuine fork.
justifications.scope_discipline: Every path in `git diff --stat 43ae5712c..0a8311e981` is inside the declared grant, and tests/standard_names/test_campaign.py:604-640 changes only the fake fetch the new pre-drain read needs.
